//: Challenge profiles (docs/gameplay-overhaul/07-challenge-outcomes.md): shared rules a step opts into with "challenge": "<id>" (or { "profile": "<id>", ...overrides }). No story chapter uses any of them yet: every existing step is legacy and plays as it always has. Each profile's top level is Captain, the default; its "difficulty" blocks give Deckhand and Brutal their own stakes (docs/gameplay-overhaul/08-difficulty-and-accessibility.md). The difficulty presets (data/difficulty) add the feel: the green, the speed, the band.

repair_graded.//: Can't fail (legacy assists stay on); reports how clean the work was. For quiet beats that should still be scored. Brutal grades harder.

repair_strict.//: A real test: no widening, two fumbles allowed. Must be won to go on (unlimited retries from the checkpoint). Deckhand allows four and calls one fumble a success; Brutal allows one.

repair_hard_choice.//: Three tries against the clock; after any failure the captain may carry on with the damage instead (a chapter adds the consequences). Deckhand: unlimited tries and more time. Brutal: two tries, two fumbles, less time.

shark_duty_strict.//: A watch that can be lost: more than three bites. Retry from the start of the watch. Deckhand allows six; Brutal one, and two failed shoves.

sash_trial_strict.//: The trial for real: lose the grip (three slips) or tear the sash and the ceremony is broken; held to the cue and let go on purpose, it's a success. Deckhand allows four slips and a slip is still a partial; Brutal allows one, tires the hands and tears sooner.

ship_repair.//: A ship repair (Pause > Ship, data/ship/integrity.json): a strict timing bar, two fumbles allowed. A failure wastes materials and the captain may try again while the materials last (the repair limits the tries), or leave it. Deckhand allows three fumbles, Brutal one.

sash_deliberate_flutter.//: The captain WANTS it to flutter early (to trigger the Stenchmaster's consequences): letting go on purpose is success, though the ceremony calls it a violation; an accidental flutter is partial; holding to the end is a failure. The intent is the same on every difficulty; only the slips allowed change.
